headline: Funding flows. Satellites soar. Propulsion preps.
deck: This week, satellite sales outpace telecom, and funding rounds keep rolling in.

stories.head: Parabilis tests propulsion, Space Force approves
stories.body: Parabilis has begun testing a hybrid propulsion system aimed at maneuverable cubesats, backed by the Space Force. This initiative underscores the military's growing interest in small satellite capabilities, which could lead to more versatile operational strategies in space. The push for propulsion technology reflects a broader trend where even the smallest players are getting a boost.
stories.soWhat: If small satellites are getting a propulsion upgrade, expect a rush to market as companies scramble to differentiate their services.

stories.head: Earth observation satellites eclipse telecom revenue
stories.body: Sales in the European space industry have seen earth observation satellites surpass telecom for the first time, marking a significant shift in market dynamics. This trend is likely fueled by increasing demand for environmental monitoring and data analytics, as companies and governments prioritize earth-centric applications. The shift suggests that the planet's health is now more lucrative than the chatter above it.
stories.soWhat: Watch for telecom companies to pivot; they might need to diversify or risk being left behind in the data gold rush.

stories.head: True Anomaly secures $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly has closed a $190 million Series C funding round, reaching a valuation of $1.6 billion. This funding round highlights the increasing importance of co-orbital security and space domain awareness, particularly in light of rising geopolitical tensions. With the DoD's backing, True Anomaly is positioning itself as a key player in the defense space.
stories.soWhat: This funding isn't just about cash; it signals a strategic pivot towards space security, which could reshape defense contracts in the coming years.

watchlist.title: Reflect Orbital's satellite tests begin soon
watchlist.body: With the FCC's approval, Reflect Orbital's satellite will soon test its sunlight reflecting technology, raising questions about its implications for astronomy and environmental monitoring.

watchlist.title: Anduril and L3Harris bid for SDA constellation
watchlist.body: Their partnership could signal a new era of tactical space operations, but only if they can convince the government of its necessity.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser launch timeline unclear
watchlist.body: Having passed its critical design review, the next steps for the Dream Chaser remain murky; delays could cost them valuable contracts.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN extension raises eyebrows
watchlist.body: The $480 million extension on the TITAN program underscores the government's insatiable appetite for data, but raises questions about the long-term strategy.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
